title: Using generative AI for visual exploration in an indie game (parallax + layered backgrounds)
author: Amezketa
selftext:
The base imagery is generated with AI, but it’s only the starting point. A significant amount of manual work goes into restructuring the output: compositing, cleanup, perspective correction, and separating elements into coherent depth layers for runtime use.

What surprised me is how well this approach holds up specifically in a parallax context.

Once the scene is broken into layers and the camera is in motion, a lot of the typical issues with generative imagery become less relevant. The brain stops reading it as a static image and starts interpreting it as spatial depth, which masks a fair amount of imperfection.

In practice, the pipeline ends up being:

* AI generation for base scene exploration
* Manual compositing and structural cleanup
* Rebuilding into layered depth slices
* Camera tuning to reinforce depth perception

Something I also found interesting: when you inspect the scene outside of its intended camera framing, everything collapses into obvious flat planes and “broken” geometry. But in motion, it reads as a surprisingly coherent environment. The illusion only works because you stop looking at the image as an image.

Curious if others are pushing similar workflows.

Demo here if you're curious:  
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/4434520/Office\_Leveling/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4434520/Office_Leveling/?utm_source=reddit)
